additional_concerns: The candidate's three-part test of accountability, effective supervision and satisfactory performance is not fully prescribed by paragraph 10. The supplied text supports continuing responsibility and substantive records and compatibility duties, but supplies no complete standard for supervision, incident materiality, duration or remediation. Identify the applicable authority and assessment-period facts before resolving satisfaction.
Section 6.11C concerns outsourced valuation. Its reasonable-care, monitoring and periodic-review requirements cannot automatically become a general tokenisation supervision standard.

Paragraph 14 directly attaches the request trigger to demonstration. Footnote 5 specifies minimum content for confirmation and demonstration without clearly resolving every timing or standard question. Absence of a request does not establish substantive compliance or eliminate confirmation.

Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition procurement of audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on SFC request. Neither procurement nor absence of a request establishes paragraph 10 fulfillment.

The supplied paragraph on proper ownership records and operational compatibility supports substantive outcomes. Missing footnote 2 and the unsupplied remainder of paragraphs 10–13 prevent treating this packet as the complete applicable standard.

Section 6.8's requested register-address disclosure and intermediary paragraph 18's prior satisfaction with controls are separate duties. Neither establishes the Product Provider's substantive discharge.

No executable meaning or operational facts are supplied. Retrieval success and the unsupported LegalRuleML result establish neither legal sufficiency nor compliance. Missing evidence must remain unresolved rather than become a negative requirement result.
